definition: A lattice model of interacting fermions with hopping terms and an on-site interaction U. It is commonly used to study correlation effects such as magnetism, pairing, and Mott physics.
notes: Project-specific sign conventions and hopping conventions must be checked in code.

definition: A correlator describing propagation or response of particles or fields. In many-body lattice simulations, equal-time and unequal-time Green functions often play different computational roles.
notes: Exact normalization, spin convention, and indexing depend on implementation.

definition: A Green-function quantity evaluated at equal imaginary time. In many DQMC codes it is central to measurement updates and equal-time observables.
notes: Precise storage convention should be checked in the code.

definition: A Green-function quantity depending on imaginary-time separation. It is often used for time-dependent correlation functions and later postprocessing or analytic continuation.
notes: Exact tensor layout and sign convention depend on the code.

definition: A correlation function of current operators. In imaginary time it is often used to infer transport quantities such as optical conductivity or dc proxies.
notes: How the correlator is normalized and which component is measured must be checked in project code.

definition: A frequency-dependent conductivity derived from current-current response. In imaginary-time simulations it is often inferred through continuation or proxy formulas.
notes: The relation between the measured correlator and the reported conductivity depends on conventions.

definition: Density of states, often referring to the spectral weight as a function of energy or frequency.
notes: If extracted from imaginary-time data, continuation details matter.

definition: Maximum entropy analytic continuation, commonly used to infer real-frequency spectra from noisy imaginary-time data.
notes: Results depend on kernel conventions, default models, grids, and regularization choices.

definition: A resampling method used to estimate uncertainty and reduce bias in derived quantities from correlated Monte Carlo measurements.
notes: Implementation details vary depending on whether bins are weighted or sign-corrected.

definition: A resampling method that generates repeated pseudo-samples to estimate uncertainty distributions of derived observables.
notes: Bootstrap usage in continuation pipelines may differ from bootstrap on raw Monte Carlo bins.

definition: A parameter controlling particle number or filling in grand-canonical formulations.
notes: Its effect on measured density depends on the model and sign conventions.

definition: Beta = 1/T in natural units. It sets the extent of the imaginary-time direction in many finite-temperature methods.
notes: Discretization into time slices also depends on dt and L.

definition: The decoupling channel used to rewrite interaction terms in auxiliary-field Monte Carlo methods.
notes: Different channels can affect sign structure and observable expressions.
